key_insight: Diamond friction depends on how passivation, surface orientation and load control interfacial bonding and whether shear stays at the interface or spreads into the softer material.
engineering_relevance: The potential enables larger-scale reactive simulations to inform diamond wear studies, chemical-mechanical polishing and ceramic interface engineering.
method: Train a reactive C/H/N/O/Si machine learning potential on diverse bulk, surface, interface and molecular structures.
Evaluate diamond reaction barriers and structural/mechanical properties of amorphous silicon nitride and silica.
Simulate diamond–silicon nitride sliding across four orientations, clean and H/OH-passivated surfaces, and loads of 0.1–23 GPa.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports validation against ab initio reaction barriers and amorphous-material properties, plus sliding simulations identifying two distinct shear regimes.
watch_item: Accuracy for untested chemistries or contact conditions requires further validation; the reported sliding study focuses on diamond–silicon nitride rather than silica interfaces.
paper_title: Development and application of a machine learning potential for diamond surfaces and their sliding interfaces with silicon nitride and silica: effect of passivation, orientation and load
